What you see: The loss climbs, bounces, or shows "nan"
Likely cause: The learning rate is too high
What to try: Lower it by a factor of ten

Likely cause: The learning rate is too low, or the walk is on a plateau
What to try: Raise the rate, or try momentum or Adam

What you see: Training stops at the step limit
What to try: Read the warning. Allow more steps or fix the scaling

Likely cause: Inputs are on very different scales

What you see: The answer hovers and never settles
Likely cause: A constant learning rate with stochastic gradient descent

What to try: Fix the seed and record it
Train from several starts and keep the best

What you see: Training loss keeps falling, new data gets worse
What to try: Stop earlier, simplify the model, or get more data

Likely cause: The model is the wrong shape, or the loss measures the wrong thing
What to try: Change the model or the loss. More training won't help
